desc:
The string words contains lowercase words separated by single commas. Choose two different entries of the list (two entries with the same text count as different words, but they trivially share letters) such that the two words have no letter in common.

Return the largest possible value of length(first) * length(second) over all such pairs, or 0 if every pair shares a letter.

words = "abcw,baz,foo,bar,xtfn,abcdef"  -> 16   ("abcw" and "xtfn")
words = "a,ab,abc,d,cd,bcd,abcd"        -> 4    ("ab" and "cd")
words = "a,aa,aaa,aaaa"                  -> 0
constraints: Words consist of lowercase English letters
hints: Comparing two words letter by letter for every pair is slow. Can you describe the set of letters of a word in a single number?
Each word uses a subset of the 26 letters, so it can be stored as a 26-bit mask. Two words share no letter exactly when maskA & maskB == 0.
Words with the same mask are interchangeable except for their length, so keep only the longest word per mask. Then test all pairs of distinct masks.
editorial: Turn every word into a bitmask: bit c - 'a' is set when the word contains the letter. Then 'no common letter' is the single operation maskA & maskB == 0, which takes O(1) instead of O(L).

Only the longest word for each distinct mask can be part of an optimal pair, because swapping a word for a longer one with the same letter set keeps the pair valid and never lowers the product. At most 1,000 masks remain, so checking all pairs is about 500,000 AND operations. Computing the masks costs O(total letters). Note that a pair of words with identical masks always shares letters, so it never needs to be considered.
time: O(total letters + m^2) for m distinct masks
